# FerroFED's self-assessment against the MyHealth@EU Requirements Catalogue
# v10.0.0 (W10-Operation Ready, 2026-03-06): one row for every requirement
# id of the catalogue, and one for its exception handling (1.25), with the
# gateway's status and the page or test that shows it. It is
# FerroFED's own reading, not a MyHealth@EU compliance check, and confers no
# Operation Ready status. The book page website/book/src/evaluate/myhealth-eu.md
# and the README badge are rendered from it by scripts/conformance/myhealth-eu.sh.
# The catalogue is privileged-access (Xt-EHR D6.1 section 5; Commission
# Decision 2011/833/EU Art 2(2)(c)) and FerroFED has no grant to reuse it, so
# this file holds requirement ids, section numbers, statuses and FerroFED's
# own conclusions, and never a word of catalogue text.
# Columns: id (the catalogue's requirement id); section (its section number
# in the catalogue); status (met, partly-met, waits-art-15-1, not-met,
# not-assessed or not-applicable), which judges the gateway's share of the
# requirement and counts every row but not-applicable as binding the
# gateway; evidence (one or more items separated by "; ", each a file of
# this repository, optionally followed by "::" and a heading of a Markdown
# file or the name of a test function of a Rust file); issue (#N, several
# separated by one space, or -);
# note (FerroFED's conclusion in its own words: what the gateway does and
# whose the rest is).
# scripts/checks/myhealth-eu.sh holds every row to the id list, the tree,
# the rendered page and badge, and the no-catalogue-text rule. No
# specification governs the form: our own design.
